subject: anatomy
title: Internal Cardiac Architecture: Crista Terminalis, Moderator Band, and Valves

steps.tx: The interior of the right atrium is divided into two embryologically distinct zones by a vertical muscular ridge termed the **crista terminalis**. The smooth-walled posterior part (sinus venarum) derives from the absorbed embryonic sinus venosus, while the trabeculated anterior part represents the true primitive atrium.
steps.say: The interior of the right atrium is split into two zones by the crista terminalis. The smooth posterior sinus venarum comes from the sinus venosus, while the ridged anterior part represents the original atrium.

vis.alt: Internal anatomy of right atrium showing crista terminalis, pectinate muscles, and fossa ovalis
vis.caption: Interior of the right atrium showing the crista terminalis demarcation and pectinate muscles. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Externally, the crista terminalis corresponds to a shallow groove on the right atrial surface designated the **sulcus terminalis**. From the crista terminalis, parallel muscular ridges known as musculi pectinati (pectinate muscles) run horizontally forward into the right auricle, resembling the teeth of a comb.
steps.say: Externally, the crista terminalis corresponds to the sulcus terminalis. Internally, parallel pectinate muscles branch off the crista into the right auricle like teeth of a comb.

left.title: Sinus Venarum (Posterior)
points: Derived from absorbed right horn of sinus venosus
Receives superior and inferior venae cavae

steps.tx: On the interatrial septum lies an oval depression, the **fossa ovalis**, representing the closed fetal foramen ovale. Bounded superiorly and anteriorly by a prominent muscular crescentic rim termed the limbus fossae ovalis (annulus ovalis), its floor is derived from the embryonic septum primum while the limbus derives from septum secundum.
steps.say: The interatrial septum features the fossa ovalis, marking the site of the fetal foramen ovale. Its floor comes from septum primum, encircled by the limbus derived from septum secundum.

Floor Becomes Fossa Ovalis; Rim Becomes Limbus

steps.tx: The right ventricle is characterized by coarse muscular trabeculae carneae and a curved muscular bundle termed the **moderator band** (septomarginal trabecula). Extending from the muscular interventricular septum to the base of the anterior papillary muscle, it carries the right bundle branch of the cardiac conducting system.
steps.say: The right ventricle features muscular trabeculae and the moderator band. Spanning from the septum to the anterior papillary muscle, it carries the right bundle branch to prevent ventricular overdistension.

rows: Leads directly to pulmonary semilunar valve
Directs inflow smoothly toward pulmonary trunk

steps.tx: Both ventricles contain **papillary muscles** projecting from the ventricular walls, anchored to the free margins and ventricular surfaces of atrioventricular valve cusps by tough fibrous cords called chordae tendineae. Papillary muscle contraction during ventricular systole tightens the chordae, preventing valve cusp eversion into the atria.
steps.say: Papillary muscles anchor to atrioventricular valve leaflets through chordae tendineae. During ventricular contraction, they pull the chordae taut to prevent valve cusps from prolapsing into the atria.

left.title: Right Ventricle Papillary Muscles
points: Anterior papillary is largest, receives moderator band
Septal papillary arises directly from septum

right.title: Left Ventricle Papillary Muscles
points: Two robust muscles: anterolateral and posteromedial
Much thicker to withstand high left ventricular pressure
Posteromedial muscle has solitary RCA blood supply

steps.tx: The posteromedial papillary muscle of the left ventricle is vulnerable to ischemic rupture following myocardial infarction because it receives a solitary blood supply from the **posterior descending artery**. In contrast, the anterolateral papillary muscle receives a dual blood supply from both the left anterior descending and circumflex arteries.
steps.say: The posteromedial papillary muscle is vulnerable to rupture after a myocardial infarction because it relies on a single blood supply from the posterior descending artery. Anterolateral papillary muscle has dual perfusion.

steps.tx: The heart valves comprise two atrioventricular valves and two semilunar valves. The **tricuspid valve** possesses anterior, posterior, and septal cusps, while the bicuspid (mitral) valve has anterior and posterior leaflets. The aortic and pulmonary valves each contain three crescentic semilunar cusps with central fibrous nodules and lateral lunules.
steps.say: The heart contains two atrioventricular valves and two semilunar valves. The tricuspid valve has three cusps and the mitral has two, while aortic and pulmonary valves each possess three semilunar leaflets.

rows: Low right ventricular systolic pressure (25 mmHg)
High left ventricular systolic pressure (120 mmHg)
High systemic aortic diastolic pressure (80 mmHg)

steps.tx: Electrical insulation between atria and ventricles is provided by the dense collagenous **fibrous skeleton** of the heart. Consisting of four fibrous rings surrounding the valvular orifices, the right and left fibrous trigones, and the membranous septum, it provides structural anchorage for valve leaflets and prevents chaotic electrical conduction.
steps.say: The fibrous skeleton provides electrical insulation between atria and ventricles. Formed by four collagenous rings and two trigones, it anchors the valve leaflets and prevents chaotic electrical transmission.
